FRAME SELECTION

Recorded viewpoints, preserved.

The whole-room sets span the full video. Chronological bins blend elapsed time (55%) with capped camera-image motion (45%); each contributes a locally sharp frame with an exposure penalty. All frames are real, distinct video frames. No interpolation or invented viewpoints.

Why the dining area? It appears from several sides during the table walk-around. The couch is mostly seen from the front. The focused set uses 34.5–37.0 and 61.0–81.0 seconds, retaining nearby furniture and walls to help camera registration. This is an area selection, not a crop or object mask.

The focused set is densely sampled, so neighboring images may be very similar. Its two time ranges can form disconnected components. Neither extra frames nor a successful reconstruction proves complete coverage; hidden backs, undersides, reflective surfaces and unrecorded angles remain limitations.

Each folder uses chronological frame_0001.png names. Frame numbers are specific to each experiment; manifest.csv maps them to the original video index and timestamp. Shared source frames use local hard links to avoid storing duplicate pixels.

Frame-count experiment settings

COLMAP / PyCOLMAP 4.2.1 · SIMPLE_RADIAL camera shared within each dataset · up to 8,192 SIFT features · guided CUDA matching · 15 neighboring images, offsets 20/40/80/160/320, and anchors every 20 images · incremental mapping and bundle adjustment on CPU · post-adjustment filtering at 4 px and 1.5° triangulation · native-size undistortion · up to 10 stereo source views · five geometric PatchMatch iterations · CPU fusion.

Matching rules use image indices, so their time spacing and pair counts change with frame count. This is a practical dataset comparison, not a strictly controlled camera-geometry experiment. The separate iPhone-aware camera-model experiment is documented on the Camera models page. Existing baseline images, models and gsplat results are preserved.

Source photographs remain local.
